s1.syndrome_frame: syndromic pigmentary retinal dystrophy with systemic features
key_facts: 39-year-old Caucasian man
no history of parental consanguinity
high bilateral myopia and nyctalopia since childhood
bilateral cataract extraction with 13D monofocal intraocular lenses 3 years earlier
moderate intellectual disability
transient neutropenia in childhood that resolved spontaneously
microcephaly
truncal obesity
joint hyperextensibility of the hands, feet, ankles, and knees
best-corrected visual acuity was 2/10 in each eye
fundus examination showed bilateral disc pallor, generalized arteriolar narrowing, mid-peripheral bone-spicule pigmentary changes, and retinal pigment epithelium atrophy

shortlist.label: Bardet-Biedl syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: syndromic pigmentary retinal dystrophy with systemic features, including intellectual disability, obesity, and joint hyperextensibility

shortlist.label: Cohen syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: pigmentary retinal dystrophy, intellectual disability, and microcephaly

shortlist.label: Alstrom syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: syndromic pigmentary retinal dystrophy with systemic features, including obesity and intellectual disability

shortlist.label: Senior-Loken syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: pigmentary retinal dystrophy and systemic features, including intellectual disability

shortlist.label: Usher syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: pigmentary retinal dystrophy and hearing loss, although hearing loss is not mentioned in the case context

raw.rationale: The combination of high bilateral myopia, nyctalopia, moderate intellectual disability, microcephaly, truncal obesity, joint hyperextensibility, and characteristic facial features such as a thick head of hair, bushy eyebrows, and a short upturned philtrum are consistent with Cohen syndrome, which is known to cause pigmentary retinal dystrophy and other systemic features described in the vignette.

rejected.label: Bardet-Biedl syndrome
rejected.why: While Bardet-Biedl syndrome shares some features like intellectual disability and retinal dystrophy, the absence of polydactyly and other specific characteristics makes it less likely.

rejected.label: Alstrom syndrome
rejected.why: Alstrom syndrome typically presents with sensorineural hearing loss and dilated cardiomyopathy, which are not mentioned in the vignette.

rejected.label: Senior-Loken syndrome
rejected.why: Senior-Loken syndrome is primarily associated with renal disease and retinal dystrophy, without the distinct facial and systemic features seen in this patient.

rejected.label: Usher syndrome
rejected.why: Usher syndrome is characterized by sensorineural hearing loss and retinitis pigmentosa, but the patient's presentation lacks hearing impairment, making this diagnosis less likely.
